ai.description: This slender snake reaches 40 cm. It is brown with a distinct pale, dark-edged vertebral stripe and a yellow collar. It features smooth scales and a small, rounded head. Family: Colubridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Gongylosoma nicobariensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, narrow pale vertebral stripe bordered by dark pigment, which is absent in other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Gongylosoma nicobariensis* inhabits the dense, humid tropical rainforests of the Nicobar Islands, typically found in leaf litter within low-elevation forest floors.
ai.behavior: The Camorta Island stripe-necked snake is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small lizards and frogs among the leaf litter of its tropical forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gongylosoma nicobariensis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, nesting likely occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Gongylosoma nicobariensis* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, occurring at low elevations within this tropical oceanic biogeographic zone.
